title: Endpoint DLP: what Microsoft Purview enforces on onboarded devices
summary: Hold: the page overstates where classification happens and extends Windows offline enforcement to devices for which Microsoft explicitly excludes that support. Its general scanning description also omits the Windows Server classification exception. Most controls and licensing statements are supported, with smaller corrections needed to clarify scoping and complete paths.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP extends Purview DLP monitoring and protection to sensitive files on onboarded Windows and macOS devices.
claims.quote: Once a device is onboarded, DLP detects when sensitive items are used and shared. This gives you the visibility and control you need to ensure that they're used and protected properly

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP supports Windows 10/11 and the three latest released major macOS versions.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) extends the activity monitoring and protection capabilities of DLP to Windows 10/11, macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices

claims.claim: Certain Windows Server versions can be onboarded for Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP allows you to onboard devices running Windows Server 2019 and later versions.

claims.where: What it is: distinction from Power Platform data policies
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP is a different mechanism from Power Platform data policies.
claims.quote: Data policies enforce rules for which connectors are enabled for each environment, and which connectors can be used together.
claims.fix: Add the Microsoft pages relied on but absent from sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/guidance/adoption/dlp-strategy for the Power Platform distinction, and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about-jit for the qualifications to JIT blocking.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified on the device
claims.claim: Files are classified on the device.
claims.quote: When you turn on advanced classification scanning and protection, the Microsoft Purview cloud-based data classification service scans items, classifies them, and returns the results to the local machine.
claims.fix: Replace the bold lead-in 'Files are classified on the device' with 'Files are classified on creation or modification'. The current wording incorrectly implies that classification stays on the device despite the documented cloud processing.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified on the device
claims.claim: A file is fully scanned for sensitive information types and labels whenever it is created or modified, without a platform qualification.
claims.quote: Installing the supported Windows Server KBs disables the Classification feature on the server. This means that Endpoint DLP won't classify files on the server.
claims.fix: Narrow the sentence to 'On Windows 10/11 and macOS, a file is fully scanned for sensitive information types and labels whenever it is created or modified.' The general statement must not include Windows servers, whose classification exception is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about.

claims.where: What it is: Files are classified on the device
claims.claim: Reading an already classified file triggers policy re-evaluation if policies, rules or sensitive information types changed.
claims.quote: When an already classified file is read, Endpoint DLP checks for any changes to the policies, rules, or SITs. If there is a change in the DLP configuration, it re-evaluates the policies and rules

claims.where: What it is: Policies are scoped by user and device; controls[0].note
claims.claim: For a Devices-location policy to be enforced, both the user and device must be in scope.
claims.quote: For a DLP policy to be enforced on an endpoint, both the user and the device must be included in the policy scope.

claims.where: What it is: Policies are scoped by user and device
claims.claim: A device needs access to all endpoint DLP policies because it can support multiple users with different policy scopes.
claims.quote: A device can support multiple user accounts. Because endpoint policies are scoped to users, different users of the device may have different policies scoped to them. Therefore, the device must have access to all endpoint DLP policies in order to evaluate items.

claims.claim: Centrally configured Endpoint settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: Rules can audit or restrict copying sensitive files to USB removable media.
claims.quote: you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to USB removable media.

claims.quote: you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to any network share

claims.claim: Rules can audit or restrict printing protected files.
claims.quote: you can block, warn, or audit the printing of protected files from an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Rules can audit or restrict copying content from protected files to the clipboard.
claims.quote: When a user attempts to copy content from a protected file, you can block, block with override, or audit the copying of protected files to a clipboard on an endpoint device.

claims.claim: Rules can audit or restrict uploads to restricted cloud service domains.
claims.quote: You can block, warn, or audit when protected files can be uploaded or prevented from being uploaded to cloud services based on the allow/unallowed domains list in Data loss prevention settings.

claims.claim: Copy or move using RDP is not supported on macOS.
claims.quote: | Copy or move using RDP | Detects when a user attempts to copy an item to a remote desktop session. | Supported | Supported | Not supported | Auditable and restrictable |

claims.claim: JIT protection blocks egress on monitored files that have never been evaluated or whose evaluation is stale until evaluation completes.
claims.quote:
Just-in-time protection blocks egress activities on these monitored files until policy evaluation completes successfully:

- Items that have never been evaluated.
- Items on which the evaluation has gone stale.
claims.fix: The cited overview supports this, but https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about-jit qualifies blocking by scope, DLP actions, allowed destinations and pause/resume support. Replace with 'JIT can block egress on monitored unevaluated or stale files while policy evaluation completes; blocking depends on user scope, DLP actions, allowed destinations and pause/resume support.'

claims.claim: Policy sync status shows whether devices received the latest policy.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Offline or unsynced devices run old policy
claims.claim: An offline device keeps enforcing the policy it already holds, without limiting this statement to Windows.
claims.quote:
When a Windows endpoint device is offline, existing policies continue to be enforced on existing files.

This functionality isn't supported on macOS endpoint devices.
claims.fix: In Why it matters, replace the offline-enforcement clause with 'an offline Windows device keeps enforcing existing policies on existing files'. In Risks and limits, replace the bullet with 'Offline Windows devices run old policy. Existing policies continue to be enforced on existing files while a Windows device is offline; policy changes reach it after it reconnects. Microsoft states that this offline functionality is not supported on macOS.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about#endpoint-dlp-and-offline-devices.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Offline or unsynced devices run old policy
claims.claim: Policy changes are not pushed to a device while it is offline.
claims.quote: DLP policies regularly sync to endpoint devices. If a device is offline, the policies can't be synchronized.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Offline or unsynced devices run old policy
claims.claim: Devices must be online for policy updates to happen.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen.
